exceptions.title: Media review by exception
exceptions.copy: Identify media items that need a closer check.
exceptions.body:
Review by exception highlights media items that need closer attention: a source to clarify, a permission to check or content changed since the last review. In this example, visual indicators help distinguish what has been examined from what still needs understanding.

For each item, check its relationship to the dossier, the scope of consent and the conditions for use. Permission at dossier level does not remove the need to check the eligibility of the specific media item. Every preparation remains subject to human review and explicit authorization before publication.

context.title: How the Context Controller works
context.copy: Understand how the dossier’s context guides the proposed actions.
context.body:
In this illustration, the Context Controller is a visual signpost connecting the current dossier, its stage and the relevant actions. It aims to explain why a suggestion appears and which information is missing before it can be considered. It presents an interface principle without connecting to a real controller.

Before following a proposed action, review the target, context and dossier status. A suggestion helps with orientation; the responsible person checks permissions, applicable conditions and the expected result, then confirms the intervention in the screen that owns the action.

human.title: AI prefill and human validation
human.copy: Prepare the information, then retain human review before taking action.
human.body:
AI prefill illustrates help with preparation: organizing information, suggesting a draft and highlighting points to check. In this guide, it is a visual principle. No connected model reads a real dossier or makes an administrative decision.

Human review means comparing the proposal with the dossier’s information, correcting facts and checking permissions. A preparation grants no additional rights. The authorized person remains responsible for the decision and explicitly confirms any sensitive action through the intended workflow.

services.title: Understanding a dossier’s service delivery
services.copy: Explore the content, consent and publication stages.
services.body:
Service delivery can be understood through three distinct stages: preparing content, checking consent and reviewing publication conditions. The dossier brings together the information needed to understand the text, media and intended destination. Each stage addresses a specific question before moving to the next.

In the illustrative journey, start by reading the content, then examine applicable permissions and anything that still needs checking. A prepared draft remains distinct from approved content. Real publication would require explicit administrative authorization for the content and its destination.

sharedWorkshop.title: A shared workshop, ideas in motion
sharedWorkshop.summary: What if a short gathering could bring different perspectives together and spark the next useful idea?
sharedWorkshop.body:
Imagine a workshop bringing together the people who support the community and those who design the tools. Each person arrives with a concrete question, an example and a possibility to explore. This fictional story illustrates one way of sharing lessons within OpenG7.

The idea is to listen before proposing, keep a short record of ideas and choose a small experiment together. Adapt this inspiration to your context; no real workshop or outcome is being announced here.

weeklyRoundup.title: A few signposts for the week
weeklyRoundup.summary: A selection of topics to revisit, ideas to explore and resources to keep close at hand.
weeklyRoundup.body:
This fictional edition brings together three perspectives: community conversations, ideas for the platform and practices for everyday work. It helps readers recover the context without browsing every section.

Start with an inspiration, open a useful resource, then return to the updates. This editorial digest represents neither real OpenG7 operations nor an audit log.

clearerNavigation.title: Clearer navigation to explore
clearerNavigation.summary: A preview of how content could be grouped to make useful reading easier to find.
clearerNavigation.body:
This demo update explores one possibility: bringing content into sections with clear roles, while retaining a way to browse by topic. Readers could find the same subject through its format or its context.

The proposal still needs to be explored with the people who would use this space. It is not an announcement of a release on the real platform.

keyboardPaths.title: Finding your way with a keyboard
keyboardPaths.summary: A few checks to make sure reading and actions remain accessible without a mouse.
keyboardPaths.body:
Start with the skip link, then move through the controls with Tab. Focus should stay visible and follow the reading order. Check that search, filters and article controls each have a meaningful name.

In a reading window, Escape should return to the content and focus should return to the original control. This demo resource offers points to check; it does not certify the accessibility of the whole platform.

listeningNotes.title: Listen to the questions before choosing answers
listeningNotes.summary: An example of a short note that preserves the context of a conversation and the questions still open.
listeningNotes.body:
A useful note can begin with what we are trying to understand. In this fictional example, the team records a navigation question, a need for context and a reading suggestion. Observations remain separate from proposed solutions.

This format makes it easier to pick up a conversation and avoids treating an assumption as a decision. No private conversation, real user feedback or personal information is reproduced here.

ideaLibrary.title: A small library of useful ideas
ideaLibrary.summary: Organize inspirations around the question they address, rather than the order they arrived.
ideaLibrary.body:
What if every inspiration answered a simple question: how to explain, welcome or find something more easily? This imaginary library favours a few ideas with context over a collection of links without signposts.

For each idea, keep a sentence about why it matters and another about what needs checking before adapting it. A saved item then becomes a way back during your visit, without approving the idea or starting a project.

shortBriefings.title: Prepare a team briefing in five minutes
shortBriefings.summary: A simple reading outline: what changed, what deserves a conversation and what to keep handy.
shortBriefings.body:
Choose a recent topic, an open question and a useful resource. Introduce the context in a few sentences and say clearly what you need from the conversation: understanding, more information or a proposal.

Finish with a signpost for what could come next, without automatically assigning an action or decision to anyone. This fictional outline can support a discussion; it creates no real task.

demoPreview.title: A preview of the new reading space
demoPreview.summary: Explore how the journal, inspirations and resources could share one starting point.
demoPreview.body:
This preview shows one way to bring useful reading closer to administrators’ daily work. The overview offers signposts, while the sections let readers focus on a type of content.

Articles, dates and authors are synthetic. Search, reading and saved items let you try the journey without connecting to real administrative data.

fieldNotebook.title: A notebook for small observations
fieldNotebook.summary: Make room for the details that could help explain a need later.
fieldNotebook.body:
An unclear label, a lengthy route, a missing explanation: small observations can support a useful discussion. This fictional notebook suggests recording them with their context and the question they raise.

An observation alone does not prove a wider problem. Bring together different perspectives before choosing a next step, and keep only the information needed to understand the subject.

accessibleStories.title: Stories you can read at your own pace
accessibleStories.summary: Take inspiration from a short, structured format that is easy to return to between activities.
accessibleStories.body:
This imaginary story starts with a clear idea, develops an example and leaves a question to consider. Short paragraphs and useful headings help readers find their place again.

The format could inspire future internal content: explicit context, concrete words and an estimated reading time. It represents neither a real testimonial nor editorial approval.

communityQuestions.title: Three questions to start a conversation
communityQuestions.summary: A new demo signpost: understand the need, share the context and imagine a next step.
communityQuestions.body:
What would help you today? What context is missing? What small possibility could be explored next? These fictional questions illustrate content added when the feed is refreshed in the demo.

They invite discussion without assuming an answer or a consensus. Refreshing adds local examples only; it does not contact an external service.

readingChecklist.title: Before sharing a resource
readingChecklist.summary: Check the context, clarity and usefulness of a reading before recommending it to the team.
readingChecklist.body:
Read the title again and check that it describes the content. Summarize its value for the team, identify what still needs confirming and make sure the text makes sense without the original conversation.

This demo signpost helps prepare a recommendation. Saving an item keeps a choice for the visit; it does not share, approve or publish any content.
